answer: Let ember, fable, and sable represent three identities in a coordinated swarm. When equivocation links k identities, pairwise evidence can trigger penalties across k(k−1)/2 pairs, so total slashing grows as O(k²), not merely with the number of offenders. Bonded escrows make those losses collectible; asymmetric capital depreciation compounds the impact, so detection of a controlled swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss and makes sybil expansion economically hazardous.
